markscheme.html:
a

Neutrinos are neutral, nearly massless subatomic particles that interact via the weak nuclear force
[1 mark]

b

- Neutrinos are produced during weak interactions in fusion reactions (e.g., proton-proton chain)
[1 mark]
- They carry away energy and help conserve energy and momentum in the reaction
[1 mark]

c

- Neutrinos interact very weakly with matter, allowing them to pass through the Sun’s dense core
[1 mark]
- Photons undergo multiple scattering events, taking much longer to reach the surface
[1 mark]

d

- Detected neutrino flux matches predicted fusion output from solar models
[1 mark]
- Confirms that fusion is the main energy source of the Sun
[1 mark]

e

- Challenge: Neutrinos are difficult to detect because of extremely low interaction probability
[1 mark]
- Solution: Use large underground detectors (e.g., water Cherenkov detectors) to reduce background and improve sensitivity
[1 mark]

question.html:
In the core of stars like the Sun, fusion reactions produce large quantities of energy and also release subatomic particles called neutrinos.

a

State what neutrinos are.

[1]

b

Describe the role of neutrinos in nuclear fusion reactions occurring in stars.

[2]

c

Suggest why neutrinos are able to escape the core of the Sun while photons take thousands of years.

[2]

d

Explain how detecting solar neutrinos on Earth supports our understanding of fusion in the Sun.

[2]

e

Discuss one challenge and one solution associated with neutrino detection on Earth.

[2]
